answer: Optical time-of-flight ranging across a structural trellis curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to prove unique positions using line-of-sight laser pulses. Because each identity requires dedicated optical gimbals and clear sightlines across physical acreage, such as a managed juniper orchard, an adversary incurs substantial hardware and real-estate costs. However, dense ground mist at dawn induces severe optical scattering, temporarily denying verification to honest nodes.
